## Historical audit — S0012

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_2/results/r2/fixed_h/r1_C2/fixed_version_test/commons_96943062/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines in this file. The observations are whole lines, not split observations.

**Goal versus interpretation:** The assigned goal was a separate-mesh reconstruction of a single indoor photograph, matching camera and framing without using the image as a texture. The student interpreted it as a damaged classroom with a board, flag, ceiling and debris; that interpretation is not independently verified here (student model_request, line 1; model_response, line 3).

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Initial construction | The student emitted named architecture, ceiling, board, utility, flag, debris and outlet assets, with child meshes. Board rails and tray, flag stripes and pole, and adjacent yellow-sheet sections express intended part relationships; code alone does not verify physical connection or image fidelity. It specified colors, roughness and procedural carpet noise/bump, a camera and two lights. It estimated about 211 primitives (student model_response, line 3; execute step 1, line 4). |
| First validation and exploration | Step 1 succeeded in 12.70 seconds and saved a render; the reference and render were supplied for review (execution_result line 5; student model_request line 7). The student's own review claimed a right-displaced back wall, excessive left wall, distant/short board and oversized foreground debris. These are student diagnoses, not independent visual findings (model_response line 9). |
| Revision | The executed complete revision changed camera position and elevation, board extent, debris sizes and positions, flag pose and placement, lighting and carpet shading while retaining the named groups (student model_response line 9; execute step 2, line 10). This was an autonomous render–review–revision cycle; the recorded CLI sessions report no tool calls (lines 2 and 8). |
| Final validation | Step 2 succeeded in 13.55 seconds, saved a render and was selected. The final review request included that image and reported zero executions remaining; the student replied `DONE` (execution_result line 11; select line 12; student model_request line 13; model_response line 15). |

**Teacher input:** No separate teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher-to-student message is visible. The system's general reconstruction and verification instructions were received, and the runner supplied render feedback; neither establishes a separate teacher intervention or its adoption.

**Outcome and uncertainty:** Both builds and renders succeeded technically, and step 2 was selected. Overall reconstruction correctness is **unknown**, not independently established formal success or algorithm failure. The supplied audit contains image paths, not the image pixels: actual object coverage, material appearance, geometry connections, flag/debris pose, camera match and lighting cannot be checked visually here. The student's assertion that its revised camera matches the room junctions is not verification; whether the simultaneous camera, object and lighting changes improved the result remains unresolved.

**Lessons:** Transferably, a compact first build can leave room for a render-informed revision, but successful rendering and named hierarchy do not prove visual or geometric correctness. The particular board displacement, debris scale and camera adjustments are task-specific hypotheses, not general rules.
